title: One request creates two tickets
description: Reconstruct a timeout and retry to find why the customer received duplicate tickets despite a low error rate.
hint: A timeout describes what the caller observed. Compare the operation keys and the destination records before deciding that a write failed.
expertReasoning: The first request committed T100 before its response timed out. The retry generated a new key and created T101. Reconcile by the original operation key, reuse that key for the same intent, and make the destination enforce deduplication atomically. Test concurrent retries and changed payloads. Resolve the existing duplicates with the owner rather than deleting records silently.

evidence.title: Customer report
evidence.body: Synthetic ticket NS-DUP. The support agent pressed Create ticket once. Two identical tickets arrived within two seconds. The UI reported a transient timeout followed by success.

evidence.title: Write path
evidence.body: Support UI → agent runtime → ticket adapter → Atlas ticket service. The adapter retries network timeouts. There is no shared transaction spanning the adapter and the service.

evidence.title: Attempt log
evidence.body:
12:00:00 attempt=1 intent=case-77 key=op-a sent
12:00:01 attempt=1 result=timeout
12:00:01 attempt=2 intent=case-77 key=op-b sent
12:00:02 attempt=2 result=201 ticket=T101

evidence.title: Destination records
evidence.body:
T100 created_at=12:00:00.400 operation_key=op-a intent=case-77
T101 created_at=12:00:01.400 operation_key=op-b intent=case-77
Both records are committed. The first response was lost.

evidence.title: Retry configuration
evidence.body:
retry_network_errors=true
max_attempts=3
operation_key=generate_new_uuid_per_attempt
Destination deduplication is atomic within (tenant_id, operation_key) and rejects changed payloads for an existing key.

evidence.title: Aggregate dashboard
evidence.body: Synthetic 24h HTTP success rate: 99.7%. Ticket-created event count: 2004. Distinct user intents: 2000. Aggregate HTTP success does not measure duplicate business effects.

causes.label: Retry changed the operation key after an ambiguous outcome
causes.explanation: Both writes committed under different keys for the same user intent.

causes.label: The user clicked twice
causes.explanation: The log records one intent followed by an automated retry; the evidence does not show a second click.

causes.label: The model hallucinated a ticket ID
causes.explanation: The destination contains two committed records, so the failure is in the write path.

remediations.label: Only increase the timeout
remediations.explanation: A longer timeout may reduce frequency but cannot eliminate ambiguous write outcomes.

remediations.label: Persist a stable key per intent, reconcile status, and test atomic deduplication
remediations.explanation: Stable identity plus destination enforcement makes repeated attempts refer to the same intended operation.

remediations.label: Automatically delete every ticket with matching text
remediations.explanation: Distinct legitimate requests may share text; deletion requires explicit business reconciliation.
